clue.text: Season with condiment, you say? But it's a roll!

indicators.note: you say signals that the phrase before it is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a season is summer and a condiment is salt, so summer salt

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to season food with a condiment, only to be told it is a gymnastic roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you say' turns SUMMER SALT (season, condiment) into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward roll heels over head is a basic tumbling move of this name.

clue.text: Go too far in some cricket function

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: Someone overdoes things at a cricket club dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is a set of six deliveries in cricket; a DO is a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaggerating or overcooking is going beyond what is right.

clue.text: Secret half of 11 broadcast little by little

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the first half of the answer to 11 across gives the letters ESTO
Eric, or Little by Little is a Victorian school novel by F. W. Farrar

explanation.surface: A secret half of something is broadcast bit by bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges ESTO, the first half of ESTONIAN (11), to ESOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by an inner circle, hidden from most.

clue.text: Vowels not doubled, do we hear, in this language?

indicators.note: do we hear asks whether the phrase spoken sounds like another word

parts.note: vowels not doubled are single Es, said as single ease

explanation.surface: A question about a tongue that avoids repeated vowels.
explanation.walkthrough: SINGLE Es, spoken, sounds like the name of the Sri Lankan tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The main tongue of Sri Lanka is known by this name.

clue.text: Experience for egghead breaking new ground

indicators.note: breaking means the letter splits into the reworked word
new says the word ground is made anew in a fresh order

parts.note: the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: An intellectual tries something fresh in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges GROUND as UNDRGO, and 'breaking' puts E, the head of 'egg', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo a trial is to go through or suffer it.

clue.text: Biting a bit of pastry

explanation.definitionFit: Sharp or acid is the adjective sense; an open pie or flan is the pastry.

clue.text: Can one carry on without his classical knowledge?

definitions.text: Can one carry on without his classical knowledge?

parts.words: Can one carry on without his classical knowledge?
parts.note: a scholar of the old Roman tongue, without whom such study could not carry on

explanation.definitionFit: A classical scholar of the Roman language is the expert described.

clue.text: Fine stuff tossed up in nets in this game

parts.note: lawn is a fine linen fabric

indicators.note: tossed up suggests the words in nets are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A fine fabric gets tossed into the nets during play.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' hints at reversal, but 'tossed up' rearranges IN NETS. LAWN is a fine linen.
explanation.definitionFit: Racket sport played originally on grass courts.

clue.text: A jolly girl Philip II sent to sea?

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cheerful girl is dispatched to sea by a Spanish king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' is a noun here: crossword slang for a Royal Marine (RM).
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish fleet of 1588 was launched by King Philip II against England.

clue.text: Famous enough once, knight is insolvent

indicators.note: the knight and the old word for enough are what is placed in the red, the container

parts.note: an insolvent person is in the red
enow is an archaic word for enough
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A once-celebrated knight has now gone bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insolvent' reads as 'in (the) red': ENOW and N go in RED. ENOW is an old poetic form of 'enough'.
explanation.definitionFit: Renowned and famous are synonyms for widely known and celebrated.

clue.text: Public school type accepting southern European

indicators.note: accepting means the pupil takes in the southern letter

parts.note: an Etonian attends Eton, the famous English public (fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: An old boy of a posh school takes in someone from the south of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is Britain's best-known fee-paying 'public' school.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a Baltic state is a European by nationality.

clue.text: Gold found by river on the rocks

indicators.note: found by places the gold beside the river in the charade

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Prospectors strike gold by a river among the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' looks like a place in the surface; it is the definition, meaning broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A business on the rocks is in ruin, lacking money: needy and broke.

clue.text: Student has ghastly time after religious expedition

indicators.note: after puts the student, ghastly and time pieces behind the religious one

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, religious
L is a learner, a student driver
grim means ghastly
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A student endures a dreadful time after a religious outing.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) is crossword shorthand for religious.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey to a holy shrine is a devout expedition.

clue.text: The English may expect his help in goal, perhaps

definitions.text: The English may expect his help in goal, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words help in goal may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper who loves England can expect English backing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines one who loves England, and 'perhaps' rearranges HELP IN GOAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover of England and things English would naturally assist the English.

clue.text: Alumnus able to read, and write, and destroy

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil
someone able to read and write is literate

explanation.surface: A former pupil, now literate, sets out to wipe things out.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out completely is to destroy.

clue.text: This dog is cross — because unsteady?

definitions.text: This dog is cross — because unsteady?

parts.words: This dog is cross — because unsteady?
parts.note: the dog is a crossbreed, and someone who staggers unsteadily might be called by the same name

explanation.definitionFit: A cross-bred hunting dog, part greyhound, bears this name, which also suits one who staggers.

clue.text: Like introverts wandering in Crete, tight-lipped at first

indicators.note: wandering means the letters of in Crete roam into a new order
at first takes only the opening letter of tight-lipped

explanation.surface: Shy people roaming in Crete keep quiet at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight-lipped' looks like the definition but only gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: Introverts tend to be reserved and uncommunicative.

clue.text: Floor comprising a numbered apartment

parts.note: an apartment is a flat
numbered suggests a number, here ten, the flat's number

explanation.surface: A floor made up of a single numbered apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor an opponent is to knock them down so they lie level on the ground.

clue.text: The novel about a fool employed in the kitchen?

indicators.note: about means the reworked word goes round the other letters
novel means new, so the word the is set out in a fresh order

parts.note: a clot is a fool

explanation.surface: A book about a simpleton who works in a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges THE as TEH, and 'about' wraps it around A CLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth for drying dishes is used in the kitchen.

clue.text: Balance the candle-end

explanation.definitionFit: A balance is what is left over; a candle stub is a leftover piece.

clue.text: Pulling back and turning in

explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawal, as of troops, is one sense; going to bed for the night is the other.

clue.text: Exerts influence to produce a book

explanation.definitionFit: Exerting influence is behaving or operating; the book is the New Testament's account of the Apostles.

clue.text: Medicine-man dividing fish in a treeless region?

indicators.note: dividing means the doctor splits the fish apart

parts.note: tuna is a fish
Dr is a doctor, a medicine man

explanation.surface: A doctor cuts up a fish in a barren landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic plains with frozen subsoil support no trees.

clue.text: Old dandy nearly swallows round biscuit

indicators.note: swallows means the shortened dandy takes the round letter inside
nearly says the last letter of the dandy is dropped

parts.note: a macaroni was an 18th-century fop or dandy
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An old fop almost gulps down a round biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts MACARONI to MACARON; 'swallows' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This almond sweet biscuit is a type of small cake.

clue.text: Outcrop, almost but not entirely stone

indicators.note: but not entirely says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An outcrop is nearly but not wholly rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A gemstone, milky and iridescent, is a precious stone.

clue.text: Boa featuring in stories by gaolbird and attorney

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or stories
a con is a convict, a gaolbird
DA is a district attorney

explanation.surface: A boa appears in tales told by a convict and a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: This large South American constrictor is a kind of boa.

clue.text: Almost universal, these taxonomic groups

indicators.note: almost says the word for universal loses its final letter

parts.note: general means universal, applying to all

explanation.surface: Biologists' classifications are nearly all-embracing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts GENERAL to its first six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological classification, groups ranking above species and below family take this plural name.

clue.text: Landlord has principal address here

parts.note: a landlord is one who lets, a letter
the head is the principal, as of a school

explanation.surface: A landlord's main address is printed here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landlord' gives LETTER, one who lets property, not a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed stationery headings show the sender's name and postal address.
